text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Glafcos Clerides clarifies his position on the United Nations proximity talks with the Turkish Cypriot side to party leaders.
- Greece appears ready to resolve its differences with Turkey, while foreign governments welcome Nicosia's decision to put Greek military overflights on hold.
- The National Council (advisory body of party leaders on the Cyprus problem) backs the government on the continuation of the proximity talks -- for now.
- U.S. basketball players plead not guilty to beating a Greek Cypriot policeman into a coma.
- Four years into the Clerides term we are back to square one concerning the Cyprus problem. Clerides's tactics on the Cyprus issue proved to be a failure.
- Some 32,000 lambs will be led to the slaughter for Easter.
- Disagreement between co-governing Diko and Disy parties on the Cyprus issue did not lead to a split in the government.
- The thermometer goes crazy. Temperatures in Cyprus have soared by 21 degrees Centigrade in just 10 days.
- Centre-right Diko party leader Spyros Kyprianou accuses Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos of switching tactics on the Cyprus issue.
